Not exactly sure how to answer. I'm in control in as many aspects of my life that I have control over, but there are so many things for which we have no control.

For the most part. I'm still stuck working, paying taxes and all that. I'd love to go live in a cabin far in the woods. I know that not entirely feasible but that's how I would feel in complete control of my life.

Within its current context, I'd say I'm in control. I do what I want, when I want, with who I want. I don't have kids so I have that freedom. I travel, scuba dive (new hobby), hunt, sport shoot, paintball, snowboard, snowshoe, etc. I work a job that pays well and is shift work, so I have the time and money. So, I guess I'm happy and in control of my life, yes.

My dream was similar ... I always wanted to buy a small farm out in the country somewhere. Over the years, it just wasn't practical ... but still, the ability to be more or less free on a plot of land large enough that i could do what i wanted without being bothered has always been an attraction.

"Want to hear God laugh? Tell him your plans".

We have the sort of control over life that you'd have in a car, equipped with summer tires, on a long winter drive in an ice storm. You do exert some control, and if you are careful and diligent you'll exert more control than if you're not; but you will surely experience skids of varying severity, at random times, and occasionally of life-alerting importance.

Being 'in control' of your life means being well-adapted to this reality. Being flexible, unafraid, able to handle the unexpected, able to change direction, and able to welcome (and exploit) each unplanned change of circumstance.
